model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Estes: a heavily Republican seat, incumbency, and an overwhelming money edge, with markets pricing a Democratic win near 7%. With no polls or expert ratings to justify moving, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a tighter race or a surge in Democratic outside spending would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ron Estes seeks another term in a south-central Kansas district that leans about twelve points Republican at the presidential level. He has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds about $1.8 million on hand, while Democrat Katy Tyndell has raised about $234,000 with under $75,000 available. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Tyndell roughly a 7% chance. Estes is the clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
